topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic on the initiation and resolution of inflammation and outlines how previous concepts will be integrated.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition and pattern recognition receptor signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system identifies microbial threats and tissue damage via molecular patterns and transmits these signals through cellular pattern recognition receptors and their pathways.

topics.label: Inflammatory mediator action, leukocyte trafficking, and systemic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how activated sentinel cells direct immune cell recruitment to inflamed tissues, facilitate lymphatic surveillance, and can drive systemic pathology such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the active and passive mechanisms that extinguish acute inflammation, the processes governing tissue repair, and the chronic outcomes that arise when inflammatory stimuli persist.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the presentation and introduces the topic of the following lecture.
